data.title: Cutaneous tuberculosis — viva
data.summary: Leprosy & mycobacterial · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Cutaneous tuberculosis** (Leprosy & mycobacterial)_

**Q1. Classify cutaneous tuberculosis.**
- Exogenous: tuberculous chancre (primary inoculation, non-immune), tuberculosis verrucosa cutis (TBVC — immune host)
- Endogenous: scrofuloderma (contiguous from lymph node/bone), orificial TB (autoinoculation, advanced disease), lupus vulgaris (haematogenous/lymphatic, high immunity), acute miliary TB, tuberculous gumma/metastatic abscess
- Tuberculids (hypersensitivity): papulonecrotic tuberculid, lichen scrofulosorum, erythema induratum of Bazin; (nodular tuberculid)

**Q2. Describe lupus vulgaris.**
- Commonest form in India; slowly progressive reddish-brown plaque with peripheral activity and central scarring (sometimes atrophic), on face in West and buttocks/extremities in India
- Apple-jelly nodules on diascopy; 'probe sign' (soft tissue — probe sinks)
- Complications: scarring, deformity, SCC (lupus carcinoma)

**Q3. What is seen on diascopy?**
- Apple-jelly nodules — yellow-brown translucent granulomas

**Q4. Describe TBVC and its differentials.**
- Warty verrucous plaque on hands/feet/buttocks (children) — 'prosector's wart'
- DDx: verruca vulgaris, chromoblastomycosis, M. marinum, sporotrichosis, hypertrophic LP, verrucous epidermal naevus, blastomycosis, iododerma/bromoderma

**Q5. What is scrofuloderma?**
- Cold abscess from underlying lymph node/bone breaks down forming undermined ulcers and sinuses with cord-like scars (neck most common)

**Q6. Investigations?**
- Biopsy: tuberculoid granulomas ± caseation (caseation prominent in scrofuloderma, absent/minimal in LV); ZN stain (paucibacillary); culture; GeneXpert/CBNAAT (rifampicin resistance), PCR
- Mantoux strongly positive, IGRA, chest X-ray, search for systemic focus (lymph nodes, lungs, bones), HIV test
- Therapeutic trial — response in 4–6 weeks

**Q7. Treatment?**
- India NTEP daily regimen: 2 months HRZE + 4 months HRE (weight-band FDCs); extend if slow response; DR-TB as per programme
- Surgery for residual scarring, plastic repair of deformities

**Q8. What are tuberculids?**
- Hypersensitivity reactions to TB elsewhere; bacilli not demonstrable but PCR may be positive; respond to ATT — papulonecrotic tuberculid, lichen scrofulosorum (lichenoid follicular papules in children), erythema induratum (nodular vasculitis on calves of women)

**Q9. Historical importance?**
- Finsen won the Nobel Prize (1903) for UV light therapy of lupus vulgaris; lupus vulgaris = 'wolf' — eats away tissue

## Quick spotter facts
- Plaque with apple-jelly nodules on diascopy — lupus vulgaris

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Cutaneous tuberculosis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.16; NTEP. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
